name: Delta Robot

speed.label: Speed (m/s)
speed.desc: Top speed of the platform along its straight path. All three axes are driven from one path parameter, so they start and arrive together.

accel.label: Acceleration (m/s²)
accel.desc: How hard the platform ramps to and from its speed. Lower it for a heavier or more delicate payload; a short move may never reach top speed at all.

commandTag.label: Command tag (job number)
commandTag.desc: Which job to run: 1 is the first job, 2 the second and so on. Set it BEFORE pulsing execute. A robot with no jobs takes a waypoint row here instead (0 is home). A number with no job or row behind it is ignored, and the platform stays put rather than guessing.

executeTag.label: Execute tag (rising edge runs it)
executeTag.desc: Pulse this false-to-true to start the job. It is edge-triggered, so holding it true does NOT repeat - drop it and raise it again for each job.

doneTag.label: Done tag (true while idle)
doneTag.desc: Handshake back to the program: true whenever the robot is ready for the next command. A job that ends on a Blend move reports done as it rounds that corner, so the next job can carry straight on. Wait for it before pulsing execute again, or the edge lands mid-job and is dropped.

enableTag.label: Enable tag
enableTag.desc: The robot moves only while this is true. Drop it and the platform brakes to a stop where it is and the job holds, timers and all; raise it and the job carries on. Wire it to the cell being safe to work in. Until a program drives it, or with it empty, the robot is always enabled, so a merely-typed tag does not hold it.

gripperTag.label: Vacuum tag
gripperTag.desc: For a robot with no jobs: grip or release the load, read continuously, so hold it true for the whole carry. A robot with jobs switches its own vacuum with Vacuum steps and ignores this.

trackPosTag.label: Tracking position tag
trackPosTag.desc: An external value that drives the platform while tracking is on: a distance sensor reading a product, or a conveyor encoder. The platform moves along the tracking direction by the change in this value since tracking began, times the scale.

trackEnableTag.label: Track tag (true follows)
trackEnableTag.desc: Follow the tracking position while this is true, for a robot driven by single moves. A job can switch tracking itself with Track steps; either one keeps it on.

trackAngle.label: Tracking direction
trackAngle.desc: The direction the tracked product travels, in degrees across the work plane: 0 is along +X, 90 along +Y (the robot's own axes).

trackScale.label: Tracking scale (m per unit)
trackScale.desc: Metres of platform travel for each unit the tracking tag changes: 1 for a tag in metres, 0.001 for millimetres. Negative reverses it, for a sensor that reads smaller as the product moves on.

in1Tag.label: Input 1 tag
in1Tag.desc: A signal a job can wait on (a Wait for step). Robots have banks of these; wire the ones your jobs use.

in2Tag.label: Input 2 tag
in2Tag.desc: A signal a job can wait on (a Wait for step).

in3Tag.label: Input 3 tag
in3Tag.desc: A signal a job can wait on (a Wait for step).

in4Tag.label: Input 4 tag
in4Tag.desc: A signal a job can wait on (a Wait for step).

out1Tag.label: Output 1 tag
out1Tag.desc: A signal a job switches (a Set step), to tell the program where it has got to. It holds its last value between jobs.

out2Tag.label: Output 2 tag
out2Tag.desc: A signal a job switches (a Set step).

out3Tag.label: Output 3 tag
out3Tag.desc: A signal a job switches (a Set step).

out4Tag.label: Output 4 tag
out4Tag.desc: A signal a job switches (a Set step).

waypoints.label: Waypoints
waypoints.desc: The places this robot knows, one row of x, y and z in metres from home: x and y across the work area, z the lowering below home (larger is lower). A place outside the work area parks at its edge. Name them, and jobs move to them by name. Pose the platform with the viewport gizmo and use Capture Pose to add one rather than typing.

blendWaypoints.label: Pass-through waypoints (robots without jobs)
blendWaypoints.desc: For a robot with no jobs: which waypoints are VIA points. The platform reports done before it reaches one, so the next move can start while it is still running and the corner is rounded instead of braked to a stop. Jobs say this on each Move step instead.

blendDist.label: Corner blend
blendDist.desc: How far before a via point the platform starts cutting the corner. Larger rounds the path more and strays further from the taught place; the robot caps it at a third of the move.

ops.label: Move
ops.desc: Move the platform to a waypoint in a straight line. Stop arrives exactly and stands still; Blend rounds the corner and carries on into the next move, for places that are only on the way somewhere.

ops.label: Vacuum
ops.desc: Switch the tool vacuum. The load is held from the step it goes on to the step it goes off.

ops.label: Wait
ops.desc: Stand still for a time, to let a grip seal or a load settle. The clock stops while the robot is not enabled.

ops.label: Wait for
ops.desc: Hold here until one of the robot inputs reads on (or off). This is how a job waits on the cell: a pallet in place, a zone clear.

ops.label: Set
ops.desc: Switch one of the robot outputs, to tell the PLC something the job has reached: clear of the table, load released.

ops.label: Track
ops.desc: Follow a moving product. On: from here on the platform rides along with the tracking position (a sensor or encoder tag), so the waypoints that follow are reached relative to the product instead of the table. Off: stop following and carry on from where the platform is. Tracking stays on across steps and jobs until a Track Off step.

jobs.label: Jobs
jobs.desc: The robot's own programs. The PLC runs one by number (the command tag) and the robot does the whole thing: moves, vacuum, waits, and the signals it sends back. While the scene runs, the step being run is highlighted.

pose.label: Idle pose
pose.desc: The place a freshly placed robot rests at, and where one waiting for its first Execute sits. It is the robot you see in a stopped scene, so set it to something that reads as parked rather than mid-cycle.
